newsitem.title: IRAQ: Russian oil minister in Iraq to discuss food sales.
newsitem.headline: Russian oil minister in Iraq to discuss food sales.

text.p: Russian Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov arrived in Baghdad on Monday to discuss oil purchases and food sales under Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.
"We want to discuss a lot of useful economic spheres and we want to know which are the useful spheres for Iraq and for us," Rodionov told reporters shortly after arriving in Baghdad.
The Russian Foreign Trade Ministry said on Thursday that its organisations were interested in supplying Iraq with 100,000 tonnes of wheat, 50,000 tonnes of sugar and other foodstuffs.

The Russians will discuss these supplies with Iraqi officials at a meeting in Baghdad from March 18-20. Iraq's Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed will represent Iraq at the meeting while Rodionov will head the Russian side.
The Russian delegation, which consists of 80 experts, also includes six undersecretaries from various ministries.

The food supplies will be delivered within the framework of the U.N. oil deal, which allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to raise money for humanitarian needs. The country is under U.N. sanctions imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

Under the pact, Russian firms have signed contracts to buy 26.2 million barrels of Iraqi oil over a six-month period from December 1996 when Iraq's oil started flowing again to international markets for the first time in six years.
Asked if he would sign new contracts with Iraq, Rodionov said: "Let us live and see after three days."
Iraqi and U.N. sources said on Monday more than 170,000 tonnes of wheat were due in Iraq in late March or early April.
